chunk_findings.detail: The new bucketing treats only `state == "running"` as "keep in full", so every job whose status is `"elsewhere"` (unended job started on another host — the state that carries the tail text "check it on that host") is pushed into `others` and therefore collapsed or dropped. That contradicts both the change's own docstring ("exited or killed jobs of OTHER items" collapse) and the README addition ("Running jobs … are listed in full"): an `elsewhere` job is *not* exited or killed, it is alive/unverifiable on another host, which is exactly the case the existing tail text exists to warn about ("WAIT for it; do not start it again" / "check it on that host"). Concrete input: `state.jobs` holds 7 unended jobs — one belonging to `B-mine`, six belonging to other items that were launched on host H2, so `J.status(j).state == "elsewhere"` for those six (this brief runs on H1). Running `ddflow brief --item B-mine` gives `keep = 0`, so all six go into `others`, `hidden = 6`, and the output is the item's own job plus the line "- _6 more unended job(s) (other items', not running): `ddflow job list` shows them…_". The alive-on-H2 jobs — and the "check it on that host"/do-not-restart warning the original code printed for each — vanish entirely, even though under the stated rule ("the item's own jobs and **running** ones in full") they should have been listed. The same misclassification bites a plain `brief`: with more than `BRIEF_OTHER_JOBS` `elsewhere` jobs, the oldest of these alive-but-unverified jobs are silently folded into the "(older, not running)" count line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py::_brief_jobs (the `s.state == "running"` classification)

chunk_findings.detail: The new partition treats only the literal state `"running"` as "must be shown in full"; every other unended state is dropped into `others`. But the status map used two lines below acknowledges a fourth state, `"elsewhere"` (tail text "check it on that host"), which is precisely a job that was started on another host and whose liveness cannot be verified from here — i.e. an unended job that may still be running. Concrete case: a job `B-other` registered on host `buildbox` is still running remotely (state `"elsewhere"`), and the user runs `ddflow brief --item B-af-signals`. With `item` set, `keep == 0`, so `B-other` is classified as an "other" and never enters `shown`; the brief emits only the count line `_N more unended job(s) (other items', not running): ddflow job list shows them...`. The job's `ELSEWHERE ... check it on that host` line and its warning are gone, and the count line asserts it is "not running" when in fact liveness is unknown/possibly live — exactly the case the docstring says is "the most expensive thing to restart by accident". Before the change every unended job was printed, so this is a new information loss for remote jobs, not just a collapse of exited/gone ones.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py — `_brief_jobs` classification `s.state == "running"`

chunk_findings.detail: `_project` creates all 40 “other” jobs with `"pid": 0` and states in the comment that this means “never running”. That premise is unsafe: `pid 0` is not a sentinel for a dead process. A standard liveness check such as `os.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for pid 0, because the call targets the caller’s process group. If the implementation detects running jobs that way, every ONE of the OTHER jobs will be classified as running; the fix’s intended behaviour is to list running jobs in full, so `Jother000` will appear in the brief and the assertion `assert "Jother000" not in text` (and the `f"{STALE} more unended job(s)"` collapse assertion) will fail on correct code. The test should use a pid that reliably raises `ProcessLookupError` (e.g., a large unused pid) or mock the liveness check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_jobs_budget.py:_project

chunk_findings.detail: The change moves every job whose status is `"elsewhere"` into the "shown in full" set unconditionally: `live = s.state in ("running", "elsewhere")` and then `shown if live or (item and j.item == item) else others`. Because `live` is ORed in, it bypasses the per-item filter entirely — a job that is on another host *and belongs to some other item* is still emitted in full, even when the brief is about a specific item. That contradicts the expected behaviour stated for this fix ("jobs of the current item (and running ones) in full, the rest collapsed to a count line naming `ddflow job list`") and re-creates the exact failure B8114a8b531 was filed for: with `brief --item B-af-signals` in a project where unrelated items have a backlog of unended jobs registered on another host (e.g. jobs added with `--pid` on a build box), all of those jobs print as `## Long-running jobs` lines ahead of the current item's section, pushing its decisions/rules/lessons past `session.brief_max_tokens` and truncating the brief. Only the `item`-matching jobs and genuinely-running jobs should be exempt from the collapse; "not checkable here" is not the same as "about the asked-for item", so the rest (including other items' elsewhere jobs) should fall into the count line.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/markdown.py:777 (`_brief_jobs`)

chunk_findings.detail: Unended jobs whose `host` differs from the local host are always rendered in full, so the crowding/truncation the fix targets recurs whenever the stale jobs came from another host — the case where the job can never receive a local `job.ended` and thus never stops being "unended". Input: 33 unended jobs of other items with `host="other"` → 33 `- **` lines before `_brief_current` → the brief is still cut at 1200 tokens before the current item's sections, and the "more unended job(s) / `ddflow job list`" collapse line does not bound them (the test shows an unrelated item's job printed in full while only the local-host ones are counted). If the fix is meant to guarantee "the rest collapsed to a count line", the collapse decision must be based on the current item plus a positive running signal, not on a host-value exemption.

chunk_findings.detail: The change promotes every unended job whose status is `elsewhere` into the fully-listed `shown` set, for every brief and regardless of which item the job belongs to. `elsewhere` is, per the added comment, the state for "not checkable here" — i.e. a job launched from another host (the same diff's README sentence is the only justification for it). Such a job is never re-resolved locally and never leaves the pending set until someone records `ddflow job end`, so on a project whose jobs are started from more than one host, the set of `elsewhere` jobs grows without bound and is *not* counted in the collapsed `hidden` line. Concretely: `ddflow brief --item B-af-signals` against a store containing 30 old `elsewhere` jobs of `fix-Ba0904a2430`, `B-dupes-sweep`, `B-onboard-*`, ... now emits 30 job lines ahead of `_brief_current`, and with `session.brief_max_tokens=1200` the brief is again truncated before the asked-for item's decisions, rules and lessons — precisely bug B8114a8b531. The same change's own README claim that "a backlog of uncollected jobs never pushes the item's own section out of the token budget" is therefore false for this class: the fix reduces crowding for locally-checkable jobs while re-opening it for jobs on another host.
